recentItems.title: Infantino says FIFA will continue to work to develop soccer, tight-lipped on sell-off questions
recentItems.description:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino attended the opening match of the Under-20 Women's World Cup in Katowice on Saturday (September 5), but kept mum on whether he regrets his abandoned proposal to sell a stake in the World Cup or plans to seek re-election next year.

    The women's Under-20 World Cup is the first tournament organized by world soccer's ruling body since the Swiss administrator called off the plan, which valued the commercial rights of the World Cup and other FIFA tournaments at $20 billion.

    The proposal was abandoned in late July in the face of a fierce backlash from regional governing bodies including Europe's UEFA and major stakeholders in the sport.

    "I'm very happy to be here in beautiful Poland, in Katowice, a fantastic city for this Under-20 FIFA Women's World Cup. It's great," Infantino said at the opener between hosts Poland and Argentina.

    "This is what we do, this is about giving opportunities, giving chances to teams, to players, to talents from all over the world, increasing number of participants."

    However, Infantino did not answer questions on whether he regretted the last six weeks after introducing the doomed proposal and if he was standing for re-election.

    "You know, there will be a lot to say, but there will be a right place and a right time to say this. It's not today. It's not here. But, here today we are enjoying football," he added.

      On Thursday (September 3), FIFA accused UEFA of launching a smear campaign and argued that its opposition to the sell off was motivated by a desire to preserve European football's dominance.

     In an indication that Infantino will fight March's election on the basis that he is best placed to continue to spread wealth to poorer nations, he also said he was "working to give every corner of the world a chance, an opportunity for dignity, to find ways and means for them to become better and to participate and to celebrate football."

    Infantino was in Katowice with senior members of FIFA including Secretary General Mattias Grafstrom, referring chief Pierluigi Collina and members of the FIFA Management Board Elkhan Mammadov and Bryan Swanson.

    Infantino arrived shortly after the President of the Polish Football Association Cezary Kulesca.

    UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin, who had previously ruled out running against Infantino, did not attend the opener.

    Some 15,000 people are expected to attend the first two matches on Saturday.    Poland face Argentina and Mexico play Benin in Katowice on the opening day.

    The event is an important development tournament in the women's game, with many of the players hoping to feature at the senior Women's World Cup in Brazil next year.

(Camera - Denis Dziuba; Editing, production and writing - Iain Axon)

recentItems.title: Tiger Woods gets 5-year license suspension in plea deal | ABS-CBN Sports
recentItems.description:
Tiger Woods will have his license suspended for five years after reaching a plea deal on Wednesday (September 2) related to his impaired-driving case.

The 15-times major champion, who initially pleaded not guilty, was present for the change-of-plea hearing when Judge Darren Steele said two five-year driver's license suspensions will run at the same time, one on a reckless driving charge and one on a careless driving citation.

"There are no exceptions. If you were to drive for any reason at all, you would go immediately back to jail," Steele told the court.

The 50-year-old Woods, who was also handed fines, has 30 days to appeal the ruling.

Woods, dressed in a dark suit and tie, arrived at the Martin County Courthouse seated in the front passenger seat of a black SUV and did not answer questions from the gathered reporters as he and girlfriend Vanessa Trump walked in and out of the building for the 8:30 a.m. ET (1230 GMT) change of plea hearing.

(Production: Pavithra George)
